cv-start.speaker: S01
cv-start.narration: Cordelia Vane does not get up. She lets you cross the whole room to her.
cv-start.text: The detective. How thrilling. Julian always said he'd be the death of someone. He never said it would be himself. What do you want to know?

variants.narration: She looks you up and down, and finds you wanting.
variants.text: Darling, have they sent you on without your script? Read your file. Then come and ask me something worth answering.

choices.label: Ask about her marriage to Crane
Ask who gains from his death

cv-night.speaker: S01
cv-night.text: I played the best second act of my life to a man who wouldn't look me in the eye, and then I took my bow alone. That's last night.

cv-julian.speaker: S01
cv-julian.narration: Something in her face closes like a fan.
cv-julian.text: Six years married, four years divorced, and ten seasons of pretending the audience couldn't tell. He was leaving for Hollywood and taking the posters with him. Does that make me a murderer, or just a woman?

cv-money.speaker: S01
cv-money.text: Follow the money, darling. It's what they do in films. Julian was insured to the eyeballs, and not in my favour. The house manager keeps the paperwork.

cv-felix.speaker: S01
cv-felix.text: Felix gets Julian's part now. And the tour, I'd imagine. Such a promising boy. Draw your own conclusions. I certainly have.

cv-voight.speaker: S01
cv-voight.text: Leonard? Harmless. He sits in Box B every opening night with a cigar he never lights and cries in the last act. Julian was his whole career.

cv-e011.speaker: S01
cv-e011.narration: She reads Mae's margin note and laughs, once, without any humour in it.
cv-e011.text: Yes, I went in. We screamed at each other for two minutes about Hollywood. Then he walked on stage with me at five past nine, alive and word-perfect, and I didn't leave that stage again until the curtain. Check the prompt book.

cv-e003.speaker: S01
cv-e003.text: There. On stage, every minute of the second act, in Harriet's own pencil. Satisfied?

cv-e010.speaker: S01
cv-e010.narration: For once, she has no line ready.
cv-e010.text: Sheldon Artists. So he'd done it. And sent Leonard a copy, the cruel little man. Eighteen years of Leonard's life, finished by carbon paper.

cv-unmoved.speaker: S01
cv-unmoved.text: And what am I meant to do with that, darling? Emote?

fm-start.speaker: S02
fm-start.narration: Felix Marsh sits on the edge of his chair, knees bouncing.
fm-start.text: Is it true they're saying I did it? Because I didn't. I was in here. I was going over the part. His part. That sounds bad. Sorry.

variants.text: I've told you about the phone call. That's everything. Honestly, that's everything.

choices.label: Ask whether he gets the part now
Ask what he saw when he came back in

fm-night.speaker: S02
fm-night.text: Green Room. Lines. The whole of the second act. I didn't go anywhere. Ask anyone.

fm-crane.speaker: S02
fm-crane.text: He was brilliant. He was awful to me. Both at once, mostly. He called me 'the spare' in front of the whole company. But I'd never — I couldn't.

fm-part.speaker: S02
fm-part.text: I — yes. I suppose I do. And the tour. That sounds terrible, doesn't it. I didn't want it like this.

fm-e004.speaker: S02
fm-e004.narration: He puts his face in his hands.
fm-e004.text: All right. All right! I went out to the payphone. Hale and Partners were casting a film, they said ring at ten to ten, and I read for them down the phone for a quarter of an hour. Ring them. Please ring them.

choices.label: Ask what he saw when he came back in

fm-corridor.speaker: S02
fm-corridor.text: When I came back in at ten past ten... the pass door at the end of the corridor was just swinging shut. Someone going back through to the front of house. I didn't see who. Just the door.

fm-e014.speaker: S02
fm-e014.text: That's a touring offer. Everyone gets those. 'Should the role become available' is just how they write them. It doesn't mean I knew anything.

fm-unmoved.speaker: S02
fm-unmoved.text: I've never seen that. Should I have? Is that bad?

hp-start.speaker: S03
hp-start.narration: Harriet Pell marks her place in the prompt book before she looks up.
hp-start.text: Stage manager. I found him. I've told the constable everything twice. What do you need?

variants.text: You haven't read the report, have you? It's all in there. I found him at 22:18. Read it, then come back.

choices.label: Ask how someone from the audience could get backstage
Ask what Crane was like to work with

hp-found.speaker: S03
hp-found.text: 22:18. He missed the curtain call, so I went myself. Door unlocked. He was on the floor between the chaise and the mirror. I touched nothing but his wrist.

hp-backstage.speaker: S03
hp-backstage.text: The pass door, between the stalls and our corridor. One key, on the front-of-house key board. You sign it out and you sign it back. If anyone came through from the audience last night, the card will say who.

hp-props.speaker: S03
hp-props.text: Brass, heavy. Props retouched the gilt at half past nine; it was drying on the table by the corridor. Anyone walking past could have picked it up. Whoever did got paint on their hands, I'd imagine.

hp-crane.speaker: S03
hp-crane.text: He had my assistant sacked last month for a cue that was two seconds late. Told me I'd be next. I'm not sorry he's gone, Detective. I'm sorry it happened in my theatre.

hp-e003.speaker: S03
hp-e003.text: Three minutes. Line fourteen snagged and nobody else would go up the ladder. Both flymen watched me do it. Ask them; they wrote it down.

hp-unmoved.speaker: S03
hp-unmoved.text: That's nothing to do with the stage. I run the stage.

lv-start.speaker: S04
lv-start.narration: Leonard Voight takes your hand in both of his. His eyes are red.
lv-start.text: Detective. A terrible, terrible night. I found that boy in a rep company in sixty-six, you know. Anything you need. Anything at all.

variants.narration: His solicitor's card is on the desk between you.
variants.text: My solicitor has advised me to say nothing further, Detective. I'm sure you understand.

choices.label: Ask who would want him dead
Tell him you know he did it

lv-night.speaker: S04
lv-night.text: Box B, as always. I watched every minute. His death scene was the finest thing he ever did. I wept. I always weep.

lv-plans.speaker: S04
lv-plans.text: Another season here, then we'd talk about London. We were renewing, you know. The papers were on my desk. I'd have done anything for that boy.

lv-enemies.speaker: S04
lv-enemies.text: I hate to say it. Cordelia never forgave him, not for one day. And the understudy gets the part now, doesn't he? I only mention it.

lv-cigar.speaker: S04
lv-cigar.text: Montecristos. I never light one inside a theatre, Detective. It's terrible manners. Julian couldn't stand the smell.

lv-lawyer.speaker: S04
lv-lawyer.narration: The warmth goes out of him like a light switched off.
lv-lawyer.text: I see. Then we're finished, Detective. You can speak to my solicitor.

lv-e006.speaker: S04
lv-e006.text: Did I step out? Nature calls, Detective, even on opening nights. Five minutes at most.

lv-e007.speaker: S04
lv-e007.narration: He looks at the initials for a long moment.
lv-e007.text: L.V.? There must be a dozen L.V.s in this building. I wouldn't know one end of that door from the other.

lv-e010.speaker: S04
lv-e010.narration: The received stamp is his own office's.
lv-e010.text: Eighteen years. Eighteen years, and he sends me a carbon copy. Yes, I knew. I'd known since Thursday. What does it matter now?

lv-e008.speaker: S04
lv-e008.narration: He looks at his own right hand.
lv-e008.text: My print? I must have picked it up. In the interval. On the props table. People touch things.

lv-e013.speaker: S04
lv-e013.text: Standard practice. Every agent insures his principal client. It would be negligent not to.

lv-unmoved.speaker: S04
lv-unmoved.text: I'm afraid that means nothing to me, Detective. Is there anything else I can help with?

md-start.speaker: S05
md-start.narration: Mae Donnelly holds the needle very still.
md-start.text: I've done nothing wrong. I was in here. Are they going to sack me?

choices.label: Ask about Crane's habits in his dressing room

md-night.speaker: S05
md-night.text: Mending. In here. The whole second act. I didn't go near Mr Crane's room.

md-crane.speaker: S05
md-crane.text: He said I took two pounds from his coat. I never. He said he'd have me out by Monday. I hope he — no. I don't hope anything.

md-habits.speaker: S05
md-habits.text: Tea at ten, every night, milk no sugar. And he hated smoke. Wouldn't let anyone smoke in his room, not even Mr Voight. He'd open the window and shout the place down.

md-e015.speaker: S05
md-e015.narration: Her voice drops to almost nothing.
md-e015.text: All right. I took him his tea at ten, like always. The door was locked. I knocked and nobody answered, and there was cigar smoke. Coming under the door. I left the tray and ran. I thought he'd have me sacked for bothering him.

md-e011.speaker: S05
md-e011.text: That's my note. They were shouting, him and Miss Vane. But he went back on stage after, I saw him go up the steps. He was fine.

md-unmoved.speaker: S05
md-unmoved.text: I don't know what that is. I just do the costumes.
